question: If the mode of a data exceeds its mean by 33.6, then the mode exceeds the median by _____. (Use empirical formula to find the answer.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Empirical relation: Mode = 3Median − 2Mean

⇒ Mode − Mean = 3(Median − Mean)

Given Mode − Mean = 33.6

⇒ Median − Mean = 33.6 ÷ 3 = 11.2

⇒ Mode − Median = 33.6 − 11.2 = 22.4

**∴ Answer = 22.4**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mode − Mean = 33.6

**Formula used:**

Mode = 3Median − 2Mean

**Calculation:**

⇒ Mode − Mean = (3Median − 2Mean) − Mean

⇒ Mode − Mean = 3Median − 3Mean

⇒ Mode − Mean = 3(Median − Mean)

⇒ 33.6 = 3(Median − Mean)

⇒ Median − Mean = 11.2

⇒ Mode − Median = (Mode − Mean) − (Median − Mean)

⇒ = 33.6 − 11.2 = 22.4

**∴ The correct answer is 22.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Formula

Mode = 3Median − 2Mean. Used for moderately skewed distributions.

Relation Derived

Mode − Mean = 3(Median − Mean)

Difference Relation

Mode − Median = (Mode − Mean) − (Median − Mean)

Use Case

Applicable when exact data is not given but mean, median, and mode are related.
